主要内容: On July 14, 2014, Abbott Laboratories announced a strategic move to sell its branded generics pharmaceuticals business (EPD) to Mylan Inc. This decision followed previous acquisitions of CFR Pharmaceuticals and Veropharm, which expanded Abbott's presence in Latin America and Russia. The sale aims to strengthen EPD by becoming a single-model business, allowing for a consistent approach across operations. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2015. Approximately 3,800 employees will transfer to Mylan, and EPD's manufacturing facilities in France and Japan will also be part of the deal. Operations in Canada, Germany, and the Netherlands will remain with EPD. This move reflects Abbott's strategy to focus on its core business and enhance efficiency. The transaction is valued at approximately $5.3 billion, based on Mylan's closing stock price on Friday. The developed markets portion of the business generated about $2 billion in sales in 2013. Abbott will retain its branded generics pharmaceuticals business in emerging markets and its other businesses in developed markets. The move is part of Abbott's strategy to focus on branded generics and improve its growth potential. On July 14, 2014, Abbott Laboratories announced that it would sell its developed markets branded generics pharmaceuticals business to Mylan for 105 million shares, or approximately 21 percent, of a newly formed entity. The business operates in Europe, Japan, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand, and generated $2.9 billion in sales in 2013. It is expected to have a sales growth rate in the upper-single to double digits. Following the transaction, which is expected to close in the first quarter of 2015, Abbott expects its sales growth rate to be 100 basis points higher, and its ongoing net income growth rate to be over 200 basis points higher. The ongoing net income associated with the developed markets pharmaceuticals business is expected to be approximately $0.22 per share in 2015. Abbott also announced the acquisition of CFR Pharmaceuticals, which is expected to be approximately $0.07 accretive to its ongoing earnings per share in 2015. The business will be reported as Discontinued Operations starting in the third quarter of 2014. The text highlights the company's forward-looking statements, which are based on current expectations and projections. It also discusses the proposed transaction between Abbott and Mylan Inc., including potential risks such as regulatory approvals, shareholder approval, and operational disruptions. The communication emphasizes the uncertainties and risks associated with the transaction, which could affect the companies' financial and operational performance.
